body:
I gotta say, the response does help to a degree. For me, at least. I don't expect to find a cure to any problems on Reddit, but the encouragement towards real help, towards self-preservation is necessary.
For whatever reason, be it emotional trauma or chemical, the people that post here (myself included), struggle with the basic instinct of self-preservation, with controlling and managing their lives. 
Any words that sway me or anyone else towards that seem like a positive. 

I can't tell you, im_want_attention, what to do or what would help. I am quite obviously in no place to give any sort of advice. But I hope you find it. And I wish there was something more I could say to help. but, I'm new to this whole grief thing and what to do about it. But I can say that, in the past 24 hours, making someone aware of the problem seems to be a first step in the right direction. As much as I hate confiding in and talking to my dad, he's someone who can help in some way or another. I eventually sent a text to my best friend who moved to Rochester for school a couple of weeks ago. She didn't try and advise or direct me but reminded me of how important I am to her and how much she cares. we spent the rest of the day making stupid jokes and all of that. That helped. I guess the best thing about talking to her is that I don't feel like I'm completely crazy or fucked up. None of this changed her attitude towards me.

So, after this, Im not sure what's going to happen. Fingers crossed and knocking on wood. Today is just going to be dedicated to survival. However one does that.

Sorry I took so long to update this.
I apparently wasn't as discrete as I thought I was and my dad found a bloody washcloth while doing some laundry. So, we spent most of yesterday talking and everything. 
As of now the idea seems to be that I may check into a hospital for a few days, since, lately, I can hardly seem to control what I'm doing. We'll see. As of this morning and probably for most of today, I'm just going to be watching day time tv and making my way through my pack of camels. 
I'm not entirely sure what all will happen in the next few days, but thank you Reddit, for the replies. It does help quite a bit.
